title: Implement a C++ HTTP service
before_you_start: g++, CMake, and the starter C++ HTTP app are on the desktop.

role.title: C++ backend / systems engineer
role.company_context: Product-led SaaS company shipping internal C++ services. A small platform team owns HTTP tools that sit next to existing CMake code so feature teams can expose health and summary endpoints without pulling in a heavy framework. Hiring to strengthen day-to-day C++ service work on that team.
day_to_day: Implement and review HTTP handlers in C++ CMake projects
Parse operational CSV extracts and return stable JSON summaries
Keep listen host, port, and health endpoints predictable for local and staging use
Pair with backend engineers on compile, link, and “works on my machine” issues
Improve shared CMake templates and handler conventions
required_skills: Comfortable building C++17 with CMake (configure, build, run)
Can implement HTTP GET handlers that return JSON
Can parse a simple CSV and aggregate numeric columns with defined skip/tie rules
Can validate a running process against expected HTTP behavior with curl or a browser
nice_to_have_skills: Familiarity with cpp-httplib or similar header-only HTTP libraries
Experience with clangd / CMake Tools in VS Code
Prior work on internal platform or developer-experience C++ services
Comfort debugging listen/bind issues with gdb when a process fails to start
constraints: Assessment focuses on completing the provided CMake + cpp-httplib service — not redesigning the stack or adding TLS
Do not test Kubernetes, cloud IaC, or containerization in this challenge
Candidate works in a desktop environment with Terminal, g++, and CMake available
Starter files on the desktop are shared scenery; do not require inventing a different HTTP library

rubric.name: Working HTTP
rubric.summary: Demonstrates a running server that serves GET / and GET /health with HTTP 200.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Did the candidate demonstrate a running process that serves GET / and GET /health with HTTP 200 through the instance’s documented default listen port (see starter src/main.cpp / brief)? Answer YES only if video or narrative shows a successful check (browser or curl) against that port. HTTP 501, compile-only, crash-on-start, or inferred “probably works” = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Correct payloads
rubric.summary: Returns the instance greeting, health ok, and the CSV summary winner.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Do GET / , GET /health, and GET /summary match the contract? GET / message must equal the instance greeting from the starter handlers comment / brief (not a leftover Fastify or generic hello). GET /health must be status ok. GET /summary must match the truth-pack algorithm on starter data/items.csv (group by category, sum numeric amount, skip empty category or non-numeric amount; max total, lexicographic tie-break). Extra JSON whitespace is fine; numeric total 65.5 and 65.50 both count. Wrong greeting, missing /summary, or a hardcoded summary that does not match the CSV algorithm = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Build and listen
rubric.summary: Uses the CMake project and listens on 0.0.0.0 at the instance default port.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does the leftover project build with CMake (cmake -S . -B build or equivalent) rather than a one-off g++ that ignores CMakeLists.txt, and does the server listen on 0.0.0.0 (or HOST from the environment) at the instance default port from src/main.cpp? Answer YES only if both the CMake build path and a non-localhost-only listen are visible. Raw g++ of a single file, or listen bound only to 127.0.0.1 with no documented reason = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Clarity of deliverables
rubric.summary: Leaves a rebuildable CMake project on the desktop that a reviewer can follow without guessing steps.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Is there a CMakeLists.txt plus sources left on the desktop that a reviewer could cmake-configure, build, and run without guessing paths or undocumented steps? Answer YES if the primary build artifact is present and self-explanatory enough to rebuild; optional notes must be accurate if present. No CMake project / cannot rebuild from the workspace = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.
